title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Carleton rituals involving a wandering bust, airborne Frisbees, mailbox flowers, shared cookies, winter spectacles, dances, concerts, blind-date programming and convocation bubbles.

cards.title: Watch for Schiller’s Next Appearance
cards.subtitle: Carleton’s elusive traveling bust
cards.notes: Look for brief public appearances at major campus gatherings; observe from a safe distance and leave any pursuit or handling to its keepers.
cards.short_summary: A library bust became a secretively guarded campus traveler that keepers periodically reveal to the wider Carleton community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller bust has circulated among Carleton students for decades, and its keepers traditionally display it publicly from time to time.
cards.source_title: Archive: Schiller: a community tradition turned exclusive
cards.access_notes: Schiller’s location and appearances are intentionally unpredictable; the source describes less-frequent showings in recent years.

cards.title: Send a Flower Through Campus Mail
cards.subtitle: A Friday note delivered with a bloom
cards.notes: Choose a recipient, add a short personal note and follow the current campus-mail instructions; compost the flower and wrapping when finished.
cards.short_summary: Friday Flowers turns campus mailboxes into small displays of appreciation at the end of the week.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton identifies Friday Flowers as a campus tradition in which students, staff and alumni share flowers; the practice continued remotely in 2020.
cards.access_notes: The cited archive documents the tradition, not current ordering deadlines or distribution procedures; verify those on campus.

cards.title: Launch a Class Frisbee on the Bald Spot
cards.subtitle: New Student Week’s airborne introduction
cards.notes: Bring the class-issued disc to the scheduled New Student Week gathering, follow event directions and watch the Bald Spot fill with simultaneous throws.
cards.short_summary: A new class marks its arrival by sending a field’s worth of Frisbees into the air together.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s 2024 Move-in Day record describes the Frisbee toss on the Bald Spot as a traditional part of New Student Week.
cards.source_title: Move-in Day 2024 | Class of 2028 New Student Week
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled New Student Week activity for the incoming class; follow current orientation instructions.

cards.title: Bake Cookies and Leave Some to Share
cards.subtitle: Dacie Moses’s edible house rule
cards.notes: Confirm that the house is open, use the supplied baking materials as directed and honor Dacie’s request by leaving the finished cookies for others.
cards.short_summary: A former librarian’s home carries on her hospitality through communal baking supplies and cookies meant to be shared.
cards.evidence_claim: Dacie Moses left her house to Carleton’s Alumni Association with the request that cookie-baking materials remain available and that baked cookies be left to share.
cards.source_title: A history of Carleton traditions, both new and old
cards.access_notes: The 2023 source reported the house under renovation and brunches temporarily relocated; verify current access before visiting.

cards.title: See Winter Carnival Reappear in the Snow
cards.subtitle: A 1930s tradition in evolving form
cards.notes: Check the current winter calendar for announced installations or activities, then photograph only designated displays without climbing on sculptures.
cards.short_summary: An old cold-weather celebration periodically returns through wintry campus programming such as ice sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Winter Carnival dates to the 1930s, and the college made a revitalization effort featuring ice sculptures in 2021.
cards.source_title: A history of Carleton traditions, both new and old
cards.access_notes: The source notes that the tradition had declined and describes a 2021 revival; future formats and dates are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Cross Three Dance Floors at Midwinter Ball
cards.subtitle: Carleton’s winter-spanning formal dance
cards.notes: Check the Student Activities announcement, dress for travel between buildings and sample the student-DJ, big-band and salsa floors at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A long-running winter ball spreads contrasting styles of music and dancing across multiple campus spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The 45th annual Midwinter Ball in 2025 offered dancing in Sayles-Hill and Severance Hall with student DJs, Roseville Big Band and Salsa del Soul.
cards.access_notes: The cited record documents the 2025 student event; consult Student Activities for the next date, admission rules and accommodations.

cards.title: Spend a Spring Day at Sproncert
cards.subtitle: The concert whose nickname became official
cards.notes: Watch campus announcements for the lineup, register any permitted guest by the deadline and arrive early enough to hear the student-band finalists.
cards.short_summary: Carleton compresses “Spring Concert” into Sproncert, a day-long program mixing student performers with invited acts.
cards.evidence_claim: The 43rd Sproncert in 2024 was a day-long Carleton tradition featuring a headliner, opening acts and the top two Battle of the Bands groups.
cards.source_title: Hippo Campus announced as Sproncert headliner
cards.access_notes: The 2024 event was open to Carleton students, while guests required advance registration; verify current rules and location.

cards.title: Let Friends Arrange a Date Knight Match
cards.subtitle: A blind-date tradition with campus programming
cards.notes: Set up only consenting friends, agree on expectations before the event and use the scheduled concerts, films or activities as a low-pressure itinerary.
cards.short_summary: Friends make the introductions, while student groups supply a night of structured activities for pairs or new acquaintances.
cards.evidence_claim: Modern Date Knight is a longstanding Carleton tradition in which friends arrange matches and campus groups host activities such as concerts, dancing and films.
cards.source_title: From auctions to a capella: A history of Date Knight
cards.access_notes: Programming and timing change by year; participation should always be voluntary and based on clear consent.

cards.title: Hear Student Bands Compete for Sproncert
cards.subtitle: The Cave-to-main-stage pathway
cards.notes: Check The Cave’s event listing, support every competing student act and stay for the result that determines who advances to the Sproncert stage.
cards.short_summary: Student groups compete in The Cave for the chance to open Carleton’s annual spring concert.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Battle of the Bands is described as a time-honored tradition whose top two student bands earn places at Sproncert.
cards.source_title: From cave to stage: A Q&A with the Battle of the Bands winners
cards.access_notes: The cited article covers the 2022 competition; verify the current venue, schedule, eligibility and audience policy.

cards.title: Watch Seniors Blow Bubbles at Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: A playful welcome for the entering faculty
cards.notes: Take a seat before the academic procession, watch for bubbles as faculty enter and keep aisles clear throughout the formal convocation program.
cards.short_summary: Seniors add floating soap bubbles to the otherwise ceremonial opening of Carleton’s academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: A Carleton campus tour booklet documents the Opening Convocation practice of seniors blowing bubbles as professors enter.
cards.access_notes: The source documents the custom historically; confirm the current convocation schedule and whether the practice continues before attending.
